items.title: Nursery teacher fined RM800 after pleading guilty to hurting autistic boy
items.summary: KLANG: A nursery teacher was fined RM800 and sentenced to seven days' imprisonment in default after pleading guilty at the Magistrate's Court today to a charge of causing hurt to a seven-year-old autistic boy last month. Magistrate Siti Zubaidah Mahat imposed the sentence on Lenah Abdul, 43, after taking into account the accused's guilty plea, as well as submissions from the prosecution and defence. The mother of five was accused of intentionally causing hurt to the autistic child at approximately 10am on Aug 28, at a special education centre for children with special needs along Jalan Bendahara, Taman Sentosa.

items.title: Sabah welcomes feedback on Mount Kinabalu accessibility
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah government welcomes constructive feedback on accessibility at Mount Kinabalu, but visitors should distinguish between facilities at Kinabalu Park and the physically demanding climb to the summit, said Datuk Jafry Ariffin. Jafry, who is Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister said the summit route was naturally steep, rocky and physically demanding, making accessibility considerations different from those involving public facilities within Kinabalu Park. "The summit route is naturally steep, rocky and physically demanding, making accessibility considerations different from those involving public facilities within Kinabalu Park," he said when contacted.

items.title: AI could pose 'existential' risk to humanity, UN rights chief warns
items.summary: GENEVA: UN rights chief Volker Turk warned on Monday that artificial intelligence could become powerful enough to threaten humanity, and said he would urge companies in the coming days to reduce the risks. Top AI companies include Meta, Anthropic, OpenAI and Google. Turk's remarks echoed prior warnings from top artificial intelligence executives themselves about extinction risks from AI, including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman.

items.title: Farmers forced to buy alternative fertiliser as Baja 3 delays persist
items.summary: KANGAR: Delays in the distribution of additional compound fertiliser (Baja 3) have forced some padi farmers in Perlis to spend their own money on alternative supplies to save their crops. Mohd Noor Hashim, 63, a farmer from Padang Besar Selatan, Kuala Perlis, said he has yet to receive the fertiliser as supplies only recently arrived at the Area Farmers Organisation (PPK) level. He said only a few farmers have received the aid so far, while stock delivered to the PPK by the National Farmers Organisation (Nafas) remains at the initial stage of distribution.

items.title: Malaysian Sikh aid team reaches remote Nepal base after 16-hour journey
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A five-member team from United Sikhs Malaysia has reached Dhunche in Nepal's Rasuwa district, near the Nepal-Tibet border, where it will establish a base camp for a humanitarian mission. According to a Facebook update, the team arrived at 11.14pm local time (approximately 1.30am Malaysian time) today, following a 16-hour drive from Kathmandu. Yesterday, the team met the Smart team and Wisma Putra officials in Kathmandu to coordinate flood relief efforts before heading to Dhunche to unload relief supplies.

items.title: Police: Missing hikers said they were in good condition when speaking to family on Tuesday
items.summary: GERIK, Sept 7 —Police said the six hikers, who are feared missing on Gunung Trans Gerah in Kelantan, were in good condition when they last contacted their family members on Tuesday (Sept 1), before continuing their journey towards Perak. District police chief Supt Abdul Samad Othman said the group last contacted their family at 7.47 am that day. “The group began their hike on Aug 29 from the Pos Dakoh area in Gua Musang, Kelantan, and were expected to make their way out via Pos Kemar, Perak on Sept 3.

items.title: Govt eyes greater pay transparency: Akmal Nasrullah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Economy Ministry is exploring mechanisms to make salary offers more transparent, giving young workers greater room to compare pay and negotiate with employers, said its minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. The ministry is also assessing the need to raise the share of employee compensation in the economy, to ensure workers' returns improve in tandem with the country's economic growth. The issue is particularly pertinent given Malaysia's median wage of around RM3,600, with Bumiputera workers continuing to record lower median incomes.

items.title: Tokyo's Shinjuku to ban more than half of holiday rentals
items.summary: TOKYO: Tokyo tourist hotspot Shinjuku will impose a ban on more than half of its holiday rentals, including homes on Airbnb, after a surge in complaints about visitors, an official said Monday. Known for its buzzing commercial and entertainment district, Shinjuku has around 4,000 short-term rentals, according to the ward's official website. A Shinjuku official supervising holiday rentals told AFP that the district was "planning to revise the current ordinance... to ban private lodging" in residential zones and areas near schools.

items.title: Tech pilgrims flock to China as global innovation race heats up
items.summary: HUMANOID robots working on factory floors, AI models challenging global rivals and electric-vehicle plants churning out cars at breathtaking scale are drawing a new wave of foreign visitors to China. He noted that visitors often arrive with misconceptions — for instance, assuming China's robotaxi sector leads the US, when domestic policy caution around potential job losses actually keeps it a step behind. China's industrial tourism sector pulled in US$17.8 billion last year, according to state media, and is projected to blow past 300 billion yuan (US$44.6 billion) by 2029.

items.title: Selangor police say investigation into Sunway Lagoon ride gone wrong to take at least three months as it waits for tech report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The investigation into the August 22 roller coaster incident at Sunway Lagoon that injured 10 visitors could take another three to four months. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said this is because investigators are waiting for technical reports from several agencies before they can wrap up the case. He said police were working with the occupational safety and health department (DOSH), Fire and Rescue Department, forensic teams and other agencies on the investigation.

items.title: 11-year-old Penang pupil strikes gold in UK public speaking contest
items.summary: In February, Aamily won a silver medal in a public speaking competition in Dubai. Education Minister and Nibong Tebal member of parliament Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said Aamily's achievements highlighted the importance of building confidence and encouraging children to embrace new opportunities. Continue to soar high, Aamily," she said.

items.title: Malaysia seeks permission to send DNA experts to Nepal - Mohamad Hasan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is seeking permission from Nepal to send Malaysian DNA experts to assist in identifying the remains of victims of the disaster, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said today. MORE TO COME © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Police arrest man for locking wife and four children inside home
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: Police have arrested a 36-year-old man for assault and unlawful confinement after he allegedly locked his wife and four children inside their home in Desa Mutiara, Jalan Gong Badak. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said police acted after receiving an emergency call from the victim, who reported that she was being abused and locked inside the house by her husband. A team from the Gong Badak police station rushed to the scene following the call.

items.title: No seat for Pakatan at annual Umno assembly, but PAS gets red carpet
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Umno will not be inviting its federal government partner Pakatan Harapan (PH) to its general assembly, starting this Wednesday to Saturday. Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said PAS was invited instead, as a reciprocal gesture for the invitation to the Islamist party’s 72nd congress in Kota Bharu, Kelantan, last weekend. “Society wants Malays to champion Malay unity — not just within Umno, but across Malay parties.

items.title: Japanese sushi chain ends Chiikawa rollout after staff caught selling freebies online
items.summary: TOKYO: A Japanese sushi chain was forced to cancel a popular marketing campaign with goods featuring cute hamster-like characters from the hit franchise "Chiikawa" after its staff stole the freebies to resell online. Conveyor-belt chain Kura Sushi launched its Chiikawa campaign on August 21 with plans to distribute a limited number of branded items like pouches and plates on a first-come-first-served basis through the end of September. Since then, Kura Sushi's stores have been inundated with calls to cancel reservations, Kosaka said.

items.title: EU still buying Russian LNG - Russian deputy foreign minister
items.summary: VLADIVOSTOK: Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) is still being supplied to the European Union, but the volumes are incomparably smaller than in the past, Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Grushko told RIA Novosti. Financial Times previously reported citing analysts that the EU had purchased nearly 10 million tonnes of gas from the Yamal LNG project from January to June 2026. The EU Council previously approved a regulation phasing out imports of Russian LNG and pipeline gas.

items.title: Zara would have remained in coma if she survived, inquest told
items.summary: The 80th witness, Mahathir Mohd Hashim @ Marikin, 45, said the doctor also told him that Zara had suffered serious injuries, including bleeding in the brain, lungs and kidneys, as well as a broken leg. "I was informed by the doctor that Zara's condition was critical. Mahathir said a doctor confirmed Zara's death at Queen Elizabeth Hospital (HQE) on July 17, 2025, while he was with the doctor.

items.title: Nepal marks national mourning day after deadly flood
items.summary: KATHMANDU: Grief-stricken Nepalis entered the traditional Hindu last day of mourning on Monday for the hundreds who died in the catastrophic flood along the country's border with China even as the government kept search operations going after four miracle rescues in recent days. Government offices in the Hindu majority nation of 30 million people and at missions abroad would fly the national flag at half-mast to mark the 13th day after death, the home ministry said in a statement. In recent days, search teams in Nepal have rescued four people, including a Chinese national who was pulled from a tunnel on Saturday.

items.title: Some Nepal villages so devastated, you’d think they never existed, says Malaysian relief volunteer
items.summary: Mercy Malaysia Rapid Assessment Team leader Vivegananthan Rajangam said some settlements along the rivers were left without a single house after the floods tore through Benighat, Nuwakot and Bidur. “In many places hit by the floods along the river, nobody lives there anymore. Vivegananthan said the Nepali authorities had also set up temporary shelters for those who survived the floods.

items.title: Toddler mauled by 5 stray dogs stable after surgery
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: A 2-year-old girl who was critically injured after she was believed to have been attacked by five stray dogs on Saturday is stable after undergoing surgery yesterday. A family member, who wished to be known only as Nur, 23, said the operation at Sultanah Aminah Hospital in Johor Baru went smoothly. Nur recounted the harrowing moments when she rescued the girl, Nur Haira Watikah Mohammad Hamizi, during the attack at about 7am.

items.title: Anwar to chair MA63 implementation action council meeting in Sabah this Friday
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to chair the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) Implementation Action Council meeting at the Sabah International Convention Centre (SICC) here this Friday (Sept 11). Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg and Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor are also expected to attend, with Sabah hosting the meeting. "For everyone's information, the MA63 Implementation Action Council meeting will be held this Friday, Sept 11, chaired by the Prime Minister and attended by the Sarawak Premier, with our Chief Minister hosting the meeting.

items.title: Two Fridays to go? Melaka CM Ab Rauf drops biggest hint yet on state assembly dissolution
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 7 — Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh today hinted that the state legislative assembly could be dissolved by the end of this month, paving the way for a state election. The Melaka Barisan Nasional chairman said the dissolution would come in “two more Fridays”, suggesting an announcement could be made within the next two weeks, Harian Metro reported. His remarks came a day after Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi urged Ab Rauf to speed up the dissolution announcement to allow the people, particularly young voters, to decide the state’s future.

items.title: Delhi court order seen as limited impact on IHH Healthcare
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Delhi High Court's order concerning IHH Healthcare Bhd's investment in India's Fortis Healthcare Ltd is not expected to have any material impact on the group's strategic plans or operations, analysts said. Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) said Fortis and IHH Healthcare remain confident that the company is compliant with applicable laws. Importantly, HLIB said no changes to Fortis' or IHH Healthcare's strategic plans are expected, while patient volumes and doctor flows remain unaffected.

items.title: Court urged to settle constitutional question before Undangs' contempt proceedings
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal should determine whether the Special Court has exclusive jurisdiction over a ruling chief before committal proceedings against six Negri Sembilan Undangs at the Seremban High Court can proceed, a lawyer said today. He said the key question was whether the term "Ruler" under Article 182 included a ruling chief and, if so, whether the Special Court had exclusive jurisdiction over proceedings involving a ruling chief. When the High Court allowed the injunction and then gave permission for committal proceedings to proceed, the question arises as to whether the High Court had encroached on the jurisdiction of the Special Court.

items.title: Umno leaves PH out of 2026 general assembly guest list
items.summary: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Pas was invited in return for the party's invitation to Umno's 72nd Muktamar in Kota Baru, Kelantan. Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki had earlier said the decision to invite Pas' top leadership was agreed upon at a party supreme council meeting. "People want to see Malay unity, not only within Umno but also among Malay-based parties.

items.title: Iran warns South Korea against involvement in Hormuz
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran's foreign ministry on Monday warned South Korea against military deployment or involvement in US operations in the Strait of Hormuz, saying such a move would have "serious consequences." On Friday, Seoul said it was considering "contributions" to US security efforts in the strategic Strait of Hormuz, which Teheran has largely controlled since the outbreak of war against the United States on Feb 28. On Monday, Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei warned South Korea against succumbing to what he called "US pressure and intimidation."

items.title: RM10,000 and a detour via Surabaya: Malaysian family stranded in Indonesia scrambles to get home after ash cloud cancels flights
items.summary: Wan Nor Ridani, 29, said his family had decided to travel by car to Surabaya before flying to Senai, Johor, as direct flights from Jakarta to Kuala Lumpur were sold out, Berita Harian reported today. The family had already bought new tickets from Jakarta to Kuala Lumpur for tomorrow, but decided not to risk another cancellation as airport operations remained subject to intermittent closures. From Senai, we will continue to Kuala Lumpur because all direct flights to Kuala Lumpur are already sold out,” he said.

items.title: Govt extends RM16bil financing to support MSMEs: Amir Hamzah
items.summary: "From the total financing, RM6 billion would be channelled through microfinancing programmes involving agencies including Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia, Tekun Nasional, Bank Simpanan Nasional, Bank Rakyat and Agrobank. "The remaining RM10 billion would be provided through the Credit Guarantee Corporation and the Small Debt Resolution Scheme via government-backed financing facilities," Amir Hamzah told the media during a visit to Media Prima Bhd's Balai Berita here today. He was received by Media Prima group chairman Datuk Seri Dr Syed Hussian Aljunid, Media Prima group managing director Datuk Mohd Rafiq Razali and Media Prima's TV Networks, Content and Primeworks Studios chief executive officer Nini Yusof.

items.title: Appeals court reserves decision on bid to stay committal proceedings against former undang Mubarak, five others
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 7 — The Court of Appeal reserved its decision on an application by six individuals, including former Undang Luak Sungai Ujong Datuk Mubarak Thahak, to stay the committal proceedings against them pending disposal of their appeal. The court also extended the ad interim stay of the committal proceedings granted to the six individuals until a decision is made on their stay application. A different three-man bench of the Court of Appeal had granted the ad interim stay on July 29 pending today’s hearing on the stay application.

items.title: Three UiTM students in hospital after endurance challenge to be discharged
items.summary: MARAN: Three of the eight Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) students hospitalised after experiencing breathing difficulties during the Komander Kesatria Endurance Challenge (KKEC) on Sept 4 are expected to be discharged today. Nine students were initially taken to hospital after experiencing health issues during the duathlon event at the UiTM Jengka campus here. Maran police chief Superintendent Wong Kim Wai said one of the remaining eight students was still receiving treatment at the Hoshas ICU and was recovering.

items.title: Missing hiking family in Kelantan mountains never stayed out more than a day, says grandpa — now it’s been four, maybe without food
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The silence from his son’s family has left Wan Zairudin Wan Ismail fearing that something may have gone wrong during their hike through the Kelantan forest. His son Wan Ahmad Aslam, 39, daughter-in-law Siti Zulaiha Norizan, 39, grandchildren Diya Raisha, 13, and Ahmad Raef, 9, and their two mountain guides have been missing since failing to emerge from the forest as scheduled last Thursday. Wan Zairudin lodged a police report at the Bukit Jelutong police station in Shah Alam two days ago.

items.title: Indonesia warns of health risks to elderly from volcanic ash
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia's Health Ministry said some 3.3 million elderly people in areas surrounding Mount Anak Krakatau, including Banten, South Lampung, Jakarta and parts of West Java, face health risks from volcanic ash, highlighting the urgency of mitigation efforts, reported Antara news agency . "The sharp silica particles contained in volcanic ash make it dangerous to the lungs, eyes and skin. Pambudi stressed that exposure to volcanic ash can cause several health problems, including acute respiratory infections, breathing difficulties, and exacerbation of asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

items.title: Police confirm RM27.5m drug syndicate crippled with main suspect shot dead
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 7 — The Royal Malaysia Police’s (PDRM) Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) crippled a drug processing syndicate suspected of producing Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) worth a total of RM27.5 million in this district and Kuala Lumpur in Op Thrips yesterday. He said the house rented by the suspect had been used as a laboratory to process the drugs since early this year, adding that police seized suspected MDMA comprising 64.49 kilogrammes (kg) of liquid, 5.2kg of drug lumps, 7.9kg of drug pills, 104.8kg of drug powder, as well as various drug-processing equipment. Hussein said the main suspect was also wanted under Section 3(1) of the Kidnapping Act 1961, in addition to having a previous criminal record under Section 448 of the Penal Code.

items.title: Fire in Indonesia's Papua kills 11, including 6 children
items.summary: JAYAPURA: A fire in Indonesia's easternmost Papua region razed a market on Monday and killed 11 people, including six children, police said. The fire was first spotted in the town of Paniai in Central Papua province shortly after midnight, and it quickly spread to several shophouses, local police spokesman Henry J. Manurung said. Authorities were still investigating the cause of the fire.

items.title: Lamborghini among 11 luxury vehicles seized in Penang
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A RM1 million Lamborghini Huracan was among 11 luxury vehicles seized in Penang after their owners failed to renew their road tax and insurance. The vehicles were seized during the Penang Road Transport Department's (RTD) Luxury operation on Sept 3. RTD said checks found all 11 vehicles had expired motor vehicle licences and no valid insurance coverage.

items.title: Shahrir Samad and Tommy Thomas discussing possible resolution of civil suit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The High Court today adjourned proceedings in the civil suit filed by Tan Sri Shahrir Samad against former Attorney General Tan Sri Tommy Thomas, former Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Latheefa Koya, and two others, to facilitate settlement negotiations among the parties. Judge Gan Techiong ordered the adjournment after Shahrir’s counsel Datuk Firoz Hussein Ahmad Jamaluddin informed the court that his client and the defendants were discussing a possible resolution of the matter. Shahrir had been scheduled to continue giving his testimony in the matter today.

items.title: Two-month-old baby among five injured in Ulu Bernam crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A family of five, including a two-month-old baby, were injured in a two-car crash along the North-South Expressway near Ulu Bernam early yesterday. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the crash, involving a Toyota Camry and a Mazda CX-5, occurred at KM440.5 of the highway towards Kuala Lumpur. "The 34-year-old male driver of the Toyota Camry suffered serious injuries and was extricated by firefighters.

items.title: [UPDATED] 'Only two more Fridays before state assembly dissolution' - Ab Rauf
items.summary: MELAKA: Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has hinted that the state legislative assembly could be dissolved by the end of this month. Speaking at the Jelajah Ketua Menteri Sayang Rakyat programme in the Sungai Udang state constituency today, Ab Rauf, who is also the state Barisan Nasional chairman, said the dissolution could come within "two more Fridays". Also present was state Senior Executive Councillor and Sungai Udang constituency development coordinator Datuk Rais Yasin.

items.title: Hadi ready to face police over US ‘topple govt’ claim, says aide
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang is expected to give a statement to police after Bukit Aman contacted him over his claim that the United States sought to help topple the Malaysian government before the 2018 general election. Hadi’s political secretary Syahir Sulaiman said the PAS president was ready to cooperate, although no date has been fixed for his statement, Berita Harian reported today. “Yes, Bukit Aman has contacted us.

items.title: Zambry tells varsities to stay alert over haze
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Higher education institutions, particularly those in Sabah and Sarawak, have been urged to closely monitor air quality amid worsening haze in the two states. Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said universities, polytechnics and community colleges had been instructed to constantly monitor the situation and comply with government directives. "We have informed higher education institutions, universities, polytechnics and also community colleges to constantly monitor, especially in the areas of Sabah and Sarawak which are more seriously affected.

items.title: MACC to grill several people over fertiliser distribution to Kedah padi farmers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is expected to begin questioning several people this week over delays in the distribution of additional compound fertiliser, or Baja 3, to Kedah padi farmers. Investigators are scrutinising information submitted by a farmers' group and reviewing information and issues raised by the Malaysian Padi Farmers Brotherhood Organisation (Pesawah), which lodged a complaint with the Kedah MACC on Aug 26. MACC had previously confirmed that Kedah MACC opened an investigation following Pesawah's complaint over delays in supplying the fertiliser to padi farmers in the state.

items.title: No new wage target, but economy minister says govt wants greater transparency in salary offers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The Economy Ministry is looking at ways to make salary offers more transparent and equitable, rather than setting an absolute wage target. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said wage growth was important to ensure the benefits of economic growth were felt by the people. Akmal said greater transparency was needed in salary offers to ensure workers received fairer returns for their contributions.

items.title: Two women remanded over alleged child mistreatment at Pahang nurseries
items.summary: KUANTAN, Sept 7 — Two women have been remanded for six days to assist in investigations into the alleged mistreatment of children at childcare centres in Kuantan and Temerloh. Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the two nursery staff, aged 31 and 26, were remanded for six days until Saturday (Sept 12) following applications by police at the Kuantan and Temerloh Magistrates’ Courts. Meanwhile, Temerloh district police chief ACP Mohd Nasyim Bahron said police received a report from the child’s 29-year-old mother at about 6 pm yesterday over allegations that her two-year-old daughter had been mistreated by a nanny at a nursery near Temerloh.

items.title: Four days overdue, rescuers mount land, air and water search for six hikers in Kelantan mountains
items.summary: GERIK, Sept 7 — Rescue teams are being mobilised by water, land and air in preparation for a search and rescue (SAR) operation for six individuals feared missing while hiking at Gunung Trans Gerah in Lojing, Kelantan. Perak Fire and Rescue Department (better known by its Malay initials JBPM) director Datuk Sayani Saidon said the department received information about the missing two mountain guides and four family members yesterday afternoon, prompting discussions with the JBPM headquarters’ operations division on the search plan. He said three boats from the Trojan Jetty in Gerik would transport eight members of the Special Tactical Operation and Rescue Team and five fire and rescue mountain guides by water to Pos Kemar.

items.title: Anthony Loke: Steps taken to strengthen checks on aviation personnel including pilots and cabin crew
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The Ministry of Transport (MOT) and the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) are taking steps to strengthen checks on pilots, cabin crew and other aviation personnel following the case involving a Malaysia Airlines (MAS) pilot linked to an international drug trafficking syndicate. Loke said MOT would definitely provide full cooperation to police, including access to airport facilities and any information or personnel required for the investigation. “The investigation is under the police.

items.title: Communications minister: Nadi-PKD synergy to optimise government resources, boost public service delivery
items.summary: CYBERJAYA, Sept 7 — Efforts to strengthen collaboration between the National Information Dissemination Centres (Nadi) and Rural Community Centres (PKD) under the Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW) reflect the government’s focus on synergy, resource optimisation and better public service delivery. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Nadi had evolved beyond providing computers and Internet access to become community information and empowerment hubs connecting people with skills, opportunities and government services. Also present were Deputy Prime Minister and Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) chairman Tan Sri Mohamad Salim Fateh Din.

items.title: Ex-Felda general manager under five-day remand as MACC digs into KL land deal
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 7 — A former Felda general manager has been remanded for five days to assist investigations into an abuse of power case involving the appointment of a developer for a project in Kuala Lumpur and the sale of land owned by the statutory body. Yesterday, MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrests and said the case was being investigated under Section 16 of the MACC Act 2009. Last week, MACC opened seven investigation papers into allegations of misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption involving Felda and its subsidiary, Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC).

items.title: Inquest told father never consulted over Zara’s autopsy
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 7 — The Coroner’s Court heard today that the father of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir was never asked for his consent regarding an autopsy on his daughter. Testifying before Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan, Mahathir Mohd Hashim @ Marikin, 45, said a doctor confirmed Zara's death in his presence at Queen Elizabeth Hospital I (HQE I) on July 17, 2025. Mahathir told the court that a attending female doctor informed him Zara was in critical condition with a broken leg and severe internal bleeding in her brain, lungs, and kidneys, adding that she would remain permanently comatose if she survived.

items.title: More than 1,000 homes from RM170,000 set to reshape Perak’s housing landscape in Meru
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 7 — More than 1,000 homes priced from RM170,000 are coming to Meru, Perak in a development that could give fresh momentum to the growing township on the outskirts of Ipoh. “We believe home ownership should be within reach of more Malaysians, especially young families and first-time buyers. He said the project in Meru Raya, with an estimated gross development value of RM291 million is aimed at young families and first-time buyers looking for more affordable homes while remaining close to Ipoh.

items.title: Transport minister: Compulsory carbon tax on aviation centre still in discussion
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Malaysia has yet to decide whether to implement a compulsory carbon tax for the aviation sector, although the country remains committed to the International Civil Aviation Organisation’s (ICAO) goal of achieving net-zero carbon emissions by 2050, said Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook. He said Malaysia would adopt a phased approach in implementing measures to reduce aviation emissions, with details to be announced from time to time. Meanwhile, the conference, hosted by Malaysia for the first time, brings together civil aviation leaders from across the Asia-Pacific region to discuss issues including aviation safety, emerging technologies and sustainability.

items.title: Education minister: Parents have discretion in having kids stay home from school if haze worsens
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Parents may choose not to send their children to school if they are concerned about their health amid the haze currently affecting the country, said Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek. "I understand parents’ concerns over the current haze situation. Fadhlina said any measures taken would be based on the National Haze Action Plan.

items.title: KLIA becomes fallback for some Jakarta flights after Anak Krakatau eruption
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Malaysia’s main international gateway in Sepang has become an alternative airport for Jakarta-bound flights after volcanic ash from the eruption of Anak Krakatau disrupted air traffic in Indonesia, news outlet Free Malaysia Today reported. Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) chief executive officer Norazman Mahmud said two flights bound for Jakarta had so far been diverted to the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) so far, with Malaysia allowing the airport to serve as a contingency gateway for affected flights. “Some aircraft bound for Jakarta have been diverted to KLIA.

items.title: Johor to shut schools statewide if API hits 200, as four districts already above 100
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Sept 7 — Johor will close all schools, kindergartens and childcare centres if the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 200 amid worsening haze. State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali today said several districts were already recording unhealthy readings this morning, with Segamat and Batu Pahat at 157, Tangkak at 153 and Kluang at 151. Dr Muhammad Naqib said schools were also monitoring outdoor activities during the current hot spell and haze, with the education department empowered to reduce such activities where necessary.

items.title: PMO: King approves end of emergency declaration in Serian
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia today consented to lift the emergency declaration in the entire Serian division, Sarawak, imposed last Friday following the haze situation. “However, the haze in Sarawak has yet to fully subside, with several areas, particularly Serian and Samarahan, still recording very unhealthy levels. According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, 40 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy levels, 24 moderate readings and two good levels.

items.title: National farmers’ group cleans house, shuts nine subsidiaries as scrutiny grows over Malaysian farm support
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — As Malaysia’s paddy farmers grapple with delays in subsidised fertiliser supplies, one of the country’s key agricultural organisations is undergoing a major overhaul after years of financial losses. Pertubuhan Peladang Kebangsaan (Nafas) – the national farmers’ organisation that supports agricultural cooperatives and distributes farm inputs – is shutting nine of its 16 subsidiaries and refocusing on agricultural inputs, its core business which accounts for more than 95 per cent of its revenue. Nafas general manager Muhammad Faris Ariffin disclosed that the national farmers’ organisation is shutting nine of its 16 subsidiaries and refocusing on agricultural inputs as part of its restructuring drive.

items.title: Four helicopter passes, 30km downstream – still no sign of Malaysians missing in flood-hit Nepal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — A helicopter search for 17 Malaysians who have been missing nearly two weeks since flash floods hit Nepal’s Rasuwa district has found no trace of the group, their belongings or the six vehicles they were travelling in. Fishtail Tours & Travels representative Roshan Panday said the helicopter made four passes over the area where the vehicles were swept away but found nothing, The New Straits Times reported today. The search team also checked a nearby forest, although it appeared unlikely that the group had managed to reach the area, he said.

items.title: Malaysian newlyweds’ Bali high turns into five-day airport nightmare, no thanks to Anak Krakatau ash cloud
items.summary: JAKARTA, Sept 7 — What was meant to be a week-long honeymoon in Bali turned into an unexpected ordeal for a young Malaysian couple after volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau disrupted their journey home, leaving them stranded in Indonesia for five extra days with limited funds. Amir and his wife were due to return to Malaysia on Sunday but found themselves stuck at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport after their connecting flight to Kuala Lumpur was repeatedly delayed and eventually cancelled. “We thought we would just sleep at the airport for a few hours and then take the morning flight home.

items.title: Penang govt auctions Tanjung Pinang land as bypass project races towards 2027 finish
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 7 — The Penang government will auction a 2.42-hectare plot of land in Tanjung Pinang next month to help Consortium Zenith Construction Sdn Bhd (CZC) secure the cash flow needed to complete the remaining works on the Ayer Itam-Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway bypass project. State Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the state agreed to auction the land after CZC sought assistance to monetise it and obtain the cash flow needed to complete the project by April 2027. He said CZC had so far claimed land worth RM695.977 million for completed works.

items.title: Stranded by volcanic ash, Malaysians in Jakarta find free beds and open arms
items.summary: JAKARTA, Sept 7 — When Anak Krakatau’s ash grounded flights across the region, seven stranded Malaysians found themselves with nowhere to go and dwindling patience. Maira Safiraa, an Indonesian who currently lives in Malaysia, opened up her Jakarta house to the group after watching the flight chaos unfold from afar. she said in a post on Threads.

items.title: No cracks in federal unity govt, says Pakatan minister as Umno closes gap with PAS ahead of assembly
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 7 — PKR today denied speculations of turmoil among federal unity government components following developments in Umno’s ties with PAS. PKR vice-president Datuk Chang Lih Kang said Pakatan Harapan (PH) continues to maintain good relations with BN, despite Umno’s strategic cooperation with PAS. “So far, there are no issues, and all Umno ministers still attended last week's Cabinet meeting.
